html:
A railway built by the French from the coast of Ivory Coast north into the interior from 1904, reaching Bouake in 1912, Bobo-Dioulasso in 1934 and Ouagadougou in 1954.

Much of it was built with forced labour. Its aim was the Niger, which it never reached. The line made Abidjan the port of landlocked Upper Volta, now Burkina Faso, and carried hundreds of thousands of Burkinabe workers south to the cocoa and coffee farms. Their descendants are a large part of the Ivorian population, and the question of who counts as Ivorian later fed the civil war.
sum: A railway built by the French from the coast of Ivory Coast north into the interior from 1904, reaching Bouake in 1912, Bobo-Dioulasso in 1934 and Ouagadougou in 1954.
